findings.highlight: notes you lent me yesterday? Think I could borrow them for a little longer?
findings.evidenceJa: 昨日の英語史のノート、もちろん取ってるよな？
findings.explanation: The student spots Haruki and asks whether he of course took notes in yesterday's English-language-history class, preparing a new request to use them. The English invents that Haruki already lent the notes yesterday and that the student is asking to extend an existing loan.
findings.japanese:
「お、いいところに！
あのさ、昨日の英語史のノート、
もちろん取ってるよな？」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, glad I caught you! Remember those English Language History notes you lent me yesterday? Think I could borrow them for a little longer?"

findings.highlight: You should at least try to take a guess before asking someone.
findings.evidenceJa: 人にものを尋ねるときはちゃんと推敲してからにしろ。
findings.explanation: Haruki tells Chiaki to revise or formulate her question properly before asking it, then deliberately answers with the time instead of the weekday. “Take a guess” neither translates that metalinguistic correction nor supports Chiaki's immediate response that she did not confuse her meaning, breaking the exchange's mechanism.
findings.japanese:
「人にものを尋ねるときはちゃんと推敲してからにしろ。
１１時だよ」
findings.todokanai: "You should at least try to take a guess before asking someone. It's 11 o'clock already."

findings.highlight: With her excellent grades and ideal learning mindset, I have no idea why she ended up coming to prep school when all she needs is just a recommendation from her homeroom teacher, however.
findings.evidenceJa:
そんなふうに成績優秀かつ授業態度も理想的、
それでいて狙いは持ち上がりの推薦だったから、
むしろ予備校に来る必然性がわからなかったけど。
findings.explanation: The source says Mihoko seeks an internal advancement recommendation, while the English invents that all she needs is a recommendation from her homeroom teacher.
findings.japanese:
そんなふうに成績優秀かつ授業態度も理想的、
それでいて狙いは持ち上がりの推薦だったから、
むしろ予備校に来る必然性がわからなかったけど。
findings.todokanai: With her excellent grades and ideal learning mindset, I have no idea why she ended up coming to prep school when all she needs is just a recommendation from her homeroom teacher, however.

findings.highlight: As if she couldn't accept what I just said, she unnaturally suppresses her expression and continues asking me questions.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺の言葉に納得したのかそうでないのか、
妙に表情を押し殺して、彼女は言葉を続ける。
findings.explanation: The source leaves open whether Mihoko accepted Haruki's explanation, while the English decides that she could not accept it.
findings.japanese:
俺の言葉に納得したのかそうでないのか、
妙に表情を押し殺して、彼女は言葉を続ける。
findings.todokanai: As if she couldn't accept what I just said, she unnaturally suppresses her expression and continues asking me questions.

findings.highlight: a fact that both myself and the company appreciated
findings.evidenceJa: ７～８時間は平気で仕事できる、両方の意味で有難いバイトがある。
findings.explanation: Haruki values this job in both respects developed around the line: it supplies a punishing amount of work and enough pay to exceed his rent. The English instead assigns the two sides of appreciation to Haruki and the company, obscuring why both workload and compensation make the job useful to him.
findings.japanese:
ここには、夜６時から出勤しても、
７～８時間は平気で仕事できる、
両方の意味で有難いバイトがある。
findings.todokanai: Even though I start work here at 6 PM, I can easily spend seven to eight hours here, a fact that both myself and the company appreciated.

findings.highlight: "Can't help it, can I? It's to save on expenses. I negotiated with each department and had the expenses split. The articles I write are the best anyway."
findings.evidenceJa:
「仕方ないでしょ。経費節約のためよ。
ちゃんと各編集部に掛け合って取材費せしめてきたし、
どうせ私が書いた方がいい記事になるに決まってる」
findings.explanation: Mari says she negotiated with the departments and extracted reporting budgets from them, while the English says the expenses were split.
findings.japanese:
「仕方ないでしょ。経費節約のためよ。
ちゃんと各編集部に掛け合って取材費せしめてきたし、
どうせ私が書いた方がいい記事になるに決まってる」
findings.todokanai: "Can't help it, can I? It's to save on expenses. I negotiated with each department and had the expenses split. The articles I write are the best anyway."

findings.highlight: I'll even throw in a raise.
findings.evidenceJa: インタビュー記事なんか全部で四か国語あるから、起こし甲斐あるわよ？
findings.explanation: Mari says the interviews span four languages, so there will be plenty worth transcribing. The English deletes the transcription task and invents an offer of a raise, changing both the work she brings back and Haruki's compensation.
findings.japanese:
「なんてね、宿題いっぱい持ち帰ったから手伝って。
インタビュー記事なんか全部で四か国語あるから、
起こし甲斐あるわよ？」
findings.todokanai: "Just kidding. I brought back a lot of work with me, so help me out. I've got interviews in four different languages. I'll even throw in a raise."

findings.evidenceJa: 就職、出版社狙ってるんですよ
findings.explanation: Haruki is aiming to find employment at a publishing company. The English changes the institution he hopes to work for into the occupation “publisher,” misidentifying his stated career target.
findings.japanese:
「経験積みたくてそうお願いしました。
…就職、出版社狙ってるんですよ」
findings.todokanai: "I requested it so that I could pack in as much experience as possible. I… want to become a publisher."

findings.highlight: Just as I was casually thinking about doing that.
findings.evidenceJa: そっちもバレてましたか。さり気なくやってたつもりだったんですけどね
findings.explanation: Haruki admits Mari has discovered that he has been taking work home, which he thought he had been doing discreetly. The English turns the completed and apparently repeated misconduct into something he was merely thinking of doing.
findings.japanese:
「あ～、そっちもバレてましたか。
さり気なくやってたつもりだったんですけどね」
findings.todokanai: "Ahh, I guess I'm busted. Just as I was casually thinking about doing that."

findings.highlight: It's an apartment that can even separate me from my mother, who might as well have been the air to begin with. A clean apartment that I've always longed for.
findings.evidenceJa:
もともと空気のようだった母親からも隔離された、
俺が求めていた無菌室。
findings.explanation: Haruki's desired 無菌室 is a sterile room sealed from interference, not merely “a clean apartment.”
findings.japanese:
もともと空気のようだった母親からも隔離された、
俺が求めていた無菌室。
findings.todokanai: It's an apartment that can even separate me from my mother, who might as well have been the air to begin with. A clean apartment that I've always longed for.

findings.evidenceJa: 女に対して培ったマメさという資質を考慮しても
findings.explanation: Haruki qualifies Takeya's attentive habit of keeping in touch as a skill cultivated through dealing with women, yet still calls him a good friend. The English replaces that specific attentiveness with simply being a massive playboy, changing the trait that explains his frequent messages.
findings.japanese:
それでもこうして頻繁に連絡をくれるあいつは、
女に対して培ったマメさという資質を考慮しても、
やっぱりいい友人って言えるんだろうな。
findings.todokanai: But the fact that he still contacts me frequently like this makes him a great friend of mine, even if I take into account the fact that he's still a massive playboy.

findings.evidenceJa: 心地良いと言うには少し深めの疲労感。
findings.explanation: Haruki's fatigue is slightly too deep to call pleasant. The English says it does feel pleasant, reversing the warning embedded in the bodily description of his deliberately extreme exhaustion.
findings.japanese:
全身を包み込む、
心地良いと言うには少し深めの疲労感。
findings.todokanai: Fatigue soon envelops my entire body, but it feels so pleasant.

findings.highlight: because these busy days are the most enjoyable to me
findings.evidenceJa: 明日もそんな忙しない…だからこそ気楽な日であることを願いながら
findings.explanation: Haruki hopes tomorrow will be similarly hectic and therefore mentally easy or carefree: constant activity prevents thought and dreams. The English says busy days are the most enjoyable to him, replacing escape-driven relief with positive enjoyment of the workload.
findings.japanese:
明日もそんな忙しない…
だからこそ気楽な日であることを願いながら、
ゆっくりと、急いで意識を閉じていく。
findings.todokanai: Hopefully, tomorrow will be as busy as today… because these busy days are the most enjoyable to me. As I pray for that in my heart, I drift off into sleep slowly but hastily.

findings.highlight: I don't dislike it, but it's painful for me
findings.evidenceJa: 『嫌い』じゃなくて『辛い』って、意味不明の反応を返すところだった。
findings.explanation: Asked whether he dislikes snow, Haruki almost answers 辛い, “painful,” instead of 嫌い, “dislike,” a one-word slip from evaluation to personal hurt. The English makes him say both that he does not dislike it and that it is painful, removing the substitution and the involuntary verbal leak.
findings.japanese:
『嫌い』じゃなくて『辛い』って、
意味不明の反応を返すところだった。
findings.todokanai: I almost let something weird like, "I don't dislike it, but it's painful for me" slip out.

findings.highlight: In my three years of studying here, this is a place I've never set foot in since changing departments.
findings.evidenceJa:
そこは、三年になり、転部してから、
ほとんど足を踏み入れたことがない場所、だった。
findings.explanation: The source says Haruki has hardly entered the area since becoming a third-year and transferring departments; the English confusingly says “in my three years” and makes the avoidance absolute.
findings.japanese:
そこは、三年になり、転部してから、
ほとんど足を踏み入れたことがない場所、だった。
findings.todokanai: In my three years of studying here, this is a place I've never set foot in since changing departments.

findings.evidenceJa: 彼女たち『政経』のテリトリーで。
findings.explanation: The café is the territory of the Political Science and Economics department, as the script itself spells out at the preceding location description. The English changes that department to Public Policy, creating an institutional and spatial inconsistency at the moment Haruki crosses into Setsuna's part of campus.
findings.japanese:
ここは、俺たち『文学部』の人間がいる場所じゃないのに。
彼女たち『政経』のテリトリーで。
findings.todokanai: This is no place for us "Literature" students. It's the "Public Policy" students' territory.
